headline: Revenue and profit grow, but taxes trim net income
summary_short: Revenue rose 2.1% y/y to $1,237.1M and operating income rose 2.8% to $464.3M, but net income attributable to Copart fell 1.0% y/y to $402.4M as other income dropped and taxes rose.
summary_long: Growth was entirely international: International revenue rose 14.1% y/y to $234.2M and International operating income rose 25.0% to $73.8M, while the US segment was roughly flat (revenue -0.4%, operating income -0.5%). Despite operating income up 2.8% y/y, net income attributable to Copart fell 1.0% because total other income dropped 26.2% (interest income -9.3%, other income swung to a small expense) and income tax expense rose 3.3%. No new guidance was issued in this release. Balance sheet: cash, equivalents and restricted cash rose to $3.35B (from $2.78B at FY2025 year-end); Copart repurchased $1.63B of stock over the nine months; stockholders' equity was $8.77B.
